hardest_step: Prove the actual fixed seed's all-order boundary expansion on the smooth physical half with complementary matrix D/N data; a smooth-double theorem is unavailable. Transfer the expansion through the common angular finite part and exact Ward/constraint reconstruction without differentiating an unsigned remainder estimate.
consequence: The actual seed trace minus its fixed inverse-distance coefficient has logarithmic bounds after every finite Euler derivative. The original reconstructed u,V have their correlated mass cubic plus O_conormal(Y^4 log Y), and the original finite completion is polyhomogeneous uniformly in its amplitude interval. Constants are finite for each fixed benchmark and order, but unevaluated. Finite-metric quantum-source derivatives and certificate admissibility are not supplied.

primary_source.title: Daniel Grieser, Notes on Heat Kernel Asymptotics (2004)
primary_source.location: Theorem 3.1, Proposition 3.8, Lemma 3.10, Proposition 3.11 and Theorem 3.12; printed pages 16, 22-24
primary_source.established_result: The Dirichlet heat diagonal has a smooth interior part and boundary profiles smooth in square-root time with rapid scaled-normal decay. The convolution class is closed, and Volterra corrections improve its order.
primary_source.extension_proved_here: For the actual constant complementary projectors, use direct-minus-reflected and direct-plus-reflected Gaussians. Left boundary conditions persist under convolution; finite matrix sums preserve the estimates. The physical half-side coefficients are smooth. The construction does not assume a smooth even double.
primary_source.does_not_supply: The paired-domain identification, full angular finite part, actual boundary coefficient, physical source cancellation, metric reconstruction or any numerical higher-order constants. The note derives these applications separately from retained inputs.

comparison: The retained proof gives numerical control only through five metric derivatives. This result establishes all finite conormal orders for its specific original family, with finite unevaluated constants. It does not promote a general C5 ball or establish a quantitative nonlinear solve. N^-5 sin(NY) rejects a uniform C5-to-C6 inference; Y^4 log Y rejects identification with ordinary boundary smoothness; Y^4 sin(Y^-2) rejects unsigned-bound differentiation.
verification_scope: Exact mixed half-space models, Mellin identities with independent 80-digit proper-time integration, Ward and constraint primitives, coordinate/completion identities and negative controls. The continuum parametrix and physical input theorems remain ordinary proofs; no actual charged heat kernel is computed.
